gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Minn Kota's '4–6 hour' charge time for its 10 A-per-bank models can cover only 40–60 Ah. The arithmetic for a 100 Ah lithium trolling battery run down to 20% (80 Ah to put back) is about 8 h at 10 A per bank, 13.3 h on 6 A banks (MK 318 PCL) and 16 h on the 5 A banks of the NOCO GEN5X3. NOCO's GEN-series manual also limits each GEN5X3 bank to batteries of up to 120 Ah, against 230 Ah per bank for the GENPRO10X series.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited Minn Kota help pages (PCL specs, and the Battery Charger Selection Guide with its 4–6 h / 10–12 h / 3–5 h charge-time column and no stated battery size), plus boatdealsdirect.com, williamswordsmith.com and sonar-wise.com. boatdealsdirect repeats Minn Kota's 4–6 h figure and gives only a 'half-charged 100 Ah at 10 A ≈ 5 h' example. williamswordsmith lists amps but no charge times. sonar-wise (a result, not cited) has the closest arithmetic: 84 Ah back at 6/10/15 A gives 14/8.4/5.6 h. But it covers only Minn Kota models and leaves out NOCO's per-bank battery-size limits (120 Ah on GEN5X3, 230 Ah on GENPRO). None of the pages notes that NOCO's amp ratings apply 'when above 0°C', or sets NOCO's 14.6 V lithium mode beside Minn Kota's 14.5 V maximum. NOCO's own spec page (cited by ChatGPT) gave HTTP 403 every time, so I could not check what it says.
decides: This removes ChatGPT's 'overnight' picks for anyone running a 100 Ah lithium battery hard. The GEN5X3 (5 A/bank, about 16 h) and MK 318 PCL (6 A/bank, about 13.3 h) won't refill a 20%-SoC battery overnight. 10 A per bank (NOCO GENPRO10X3 or Minn Kota MK 330 PCL, about 8 h) is the minimum for an overnight refill. For back-to-back fishing days, 15 A per bank (MK 345 PCL, about 5.3 h) is the pick, but Minn Kota sizes a generator for it at 700 W against 450 W for the MK 330 PCL. On lithium voltage, the GENPRO10X3 (14.6 V) and Minn Kota PCL (14.5 V max) are effectively the same, so voltage does not separate them.
